subject: Can I assign more than 3 columns to lodcolumn and if yes, how?

messages.author: b862418127f8a2ba
messages.subject: Can I assign more than 3 columns to lodcolumn and if yes, how?
parts:
Hi Karl, 

I am running a QTL analysis with 20 different wheat phenotypes and would want to plot the LOD profiles of all simultaneously. 

Below is the code I'm using for the plots, z is the summary of the scaneone (with 1000 permutations). As a next step I want to make a pdf file with one plot for each phenotype, so 20 plots in one file. 

z<-summary(cross.sc1.perms, alpha=.05)
pdf(file="12_QTL Plots.pdf", width=11, height=8.5)
for(i in 2:nphe(cross)){
  plot(cross.sc1, lodcolumn=i, lwd=1.5, gap=0, bandcol="gray70", incl.markers=TRUE, ylab="LOD", main=colnames(cross$pheno[i]), xlab=c("Threshold for alpha=.05 using 1000 permutations", z[i]))
  add.threshold(cross.sc1, perms=cross.sc1.perms, alpha=0.05, lodcolumn=i, gap=0)
}


I keep gettingError in plot.scanone(qtl.sc1, lodcolumn = i, lwd = 1.5, gap = 0, bandcol = "gray70", : 
  Argument lodcolumn misspecified.
Can I not define lodcolumn this way? 

Thanks, 
Sandra

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Can I assign more than 3 columns to lodcolumn and if yes, how?
parts:
It should work just as you've done it, but the error "Argument lodcolumn misspecified" indicates that you're pointing to a column that doesn't exist.

Try

ncol(cross.sc1)

to see how many columns there are in cross.sc1. If there are 8 columns (which includes the columns for chromosome and position) than lodcolumn would need to be between 1 and 6.

karl
